<div class="jsr">
<header class="jsr-header" id="jsr-top">
<p class="jsr-kicker">HerPath &middot; 2026 JumpStart Challenge</p>
<h1 class="jsr-title">Helping more women-founded companies in Lincoln get funded and grow: the research</h1>
<p class="jsr-sub">The evidence behind our pitch, what our Lincoln pilot survey heard, and the wider research we read.</p>
</header>
<nav class="jsr-toc" aria-label="On this page">
<ol>
<li><a href="#highlights">Highlights</a></li>
<li><a href="#cited">Research cited in the pitch</a></li>
<li><a href="#survey">Survey results</a></li>
<li><a href="#rest">The rest of the research</a></li>
<li><a href="#sources">Sources</a></li>
</ol>
</nav>
<div class="jsr-main">
<section id="highlights" class="page-section" aria-labelledby="highlights-heading">
<h2 id="highlights-heading">Highlights</h2>
<p class="section-intro">Seven findings from across this page.
Each links to a card further down; open the card for the detail, the source and how strong the evidence is.</p>
<ol class="highlights">
<li class="hl">
<p class="hl-figure">11% <span class="hl-vs">vs</span> 23%</p>
<p class="hl-text"><a href="#cited-hiring">Only 11% of women-owned Nebraska businesses have employees, against 23% of men-owned.</a><sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-1" id="fnref-1-1" aria-label="Source 1">1</a></sup>
Lincoln shows the same gap: <a href="#rest-local-lincoln">13% against 23%</a>.<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-2" id="fnref-2-1" aria-label="Source 2">2</a></sup></p>
</li>
<li class="hl">
<p class="hl-figure">27% <span class="hl-vs">vs</span> 23%</p>
<p class="hl-text"><a href="#cited-angels">When women's deals reach US angel investors, 27% get funded, against 23% of all deals.</a><sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-3" id="fnref-3-1" aria-label="Source 3">3</a></sup>
The comparison is with the whole market, not with men's deals alone.</p>
</li>
<li class="hl">
<p class="hl-figure">78%</p>
<p class="hl-text"><a href="#rest-capital-not-applying">Most women-owned employer firms did not ask for credit: 78% did not apply for new credit in 2024.</a><sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-4" id="fnref-4-1" aria-label="Source 4">4</a></sup>
Once they apply, <a href="#rest-evidence-approval">women's full-approval rate is close to men's</a> (49% against 52% in 2025).<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-5" id="fnref-5-1" aria-label="Source 5">5</a></sup></p>
</li>
<li class="hl">
<p class="hl-figure">Who invests</p>
<p class="hl-text"><a href="#rest-evidence-women-investors">More women writing checks moved money to women founders.</a><sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-6" id="fnref-6-1" aria-label="Source 6">6</a></sup>
When US venture firms hired more women investors, the share of funded founders who were women rose; male investors did not become more likely to back women.</p>
</li>
<li class="hl">
<p class="hl-figure">18 of 33</p>
<p class="hl-text"><a href="#survey-f1">In our pilot survey, the connection people wish for most is a mentor who has done it before.</a><sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-7" id="fnref-7-1" aria-label="Source 7">7</a></sup></p>
</li>
<li class="hl">
<p class="hl-figure">14 of 26</p>
<p class="hl-text"><a href="#survey-f2">The top reason a wanted connection did not happen: &ldquo;I didn't know who the right person was.&rdquo;</a><sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-7" id="fnref-7-2" aria-label="Source 7">7</a></sup></p>
</li>
<li class="hl">
<p class="hl-figure">10 of 21 women</p>
<p class="hl-text"><a href="#survey-f5">Caregiving takes up time for 10 of 21 women who answered, and for fewer than 3 of 19 men.</a><sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-7" id="fnref-7-3" aria-label="Source 7">7</a></sup></p>
</li>
</ol>
<p class="note">The survey figures come from a small pilot that reached the team's own contacts; read them as illustrations, not estimates for Lincoln. See <a href="#survey-limits">what the survey can and cannot tell us</a>.</p>
</section>

<p class="note to-top"><a href="#jsr-top">Back to top</a></p>
<section id="cited" class="page-section" aria-labelledby="cited-heading">
<h2 id="cited-heading">Research cited in the pitch</h2>
<p class="section-intro">These are the six facts our pitch rests on, in the order we say them.
Open a card to see where each figure comes from, where to find it in the source, and how we checked it.
Where our pitch wording says more than the source does, the card says so.</p>

<details class="card" id="cited-women-own">
<summary>Women own <strong>44%</strong> of Nebraska businesses<sup class="fn" aria-hidden="true">1</sup></summary>
<p><strong>In the pitch:</strong> the spoken script opens with "Women own 44% of Nebraska businesses."</p>
<p><strong>What the source says:</strong> the U.S. Small Business Administration's 2025 profile of Nebraska says women made up 47% of workers and owned 44% of businesses.<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-1" id="fnref-1-2" aria-label="Source 1">1</a></sup>
The figures come from Census surveys of 2022.</p>
<p><strong>Where to find it:</strong> page 3 of the profile, in the part on business ownership share by demographic group.</p>
<p><strong>How we checked:</strong> <span class="status status-checked">Checked</span> We read the figure in our saved copy of the profile PDF.</p>
<p><strong>Read with care:</strong> the profile notes that "Ownership shares include equal and majority ownership."
So the 44% counts businesses owned equally by a woman and a man as well as those mostly owned by women.
Counting only businesses owned mostly by women, the share is about 37% (our arithmetic from the profile's table: 67,994 of the 185,360 businesses with an owner's sex recorded).<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-1" id="fnref-1-3" aria-label="Source 1">1</a></sup></p>
</details>

<details class="card" id="cited-hiring">
<summary>Only <strong>11%</strong> of women-owned Nebraska businesses have employees; for men it is <strong>23%</strong>, about double<sup class="fn" aria-hidden="true">1</sup></summary>
<p><strong>In the pitch:</strong> slide 2 says "Only 11% of women-owned businesses in Nebraska grow to the point of hiring anyone. For men, it's double that."
The script adds the men's figure: twenty-three percent, and says the pilot survey is too small to test that gap.</p>
<p><strong>What the source says:</strong> of 67,994 Nebraska businesses owned by women, 7,494 (11%) have employees.
Of 103,863 owned by men, 23,363 (23%) do.<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-1" id="fnref-1-4" aria-label="Source 1">1</a></sup>
Of 13,503 owned equally by women and men, 7,103 (53%) have employees.<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-1" id="fnref-1-5" aria-label="Source 1">1</a></sup>
23% is a little more than twice 11%.
The figures are for 2022.</p>
<p><strong>Where to find it:</strong> page 3 of the profile, in the table of business counts by owner demographic group or location type, rows Female and Male, and the row below them for businesses owned equally by both groups.</p>
<p><strong>How we checked:</strong> <span class="status status-checked">Checked</span> We read both rows in our saved copy of the profile PDF.
We read the equally owned row there too.
Newer Census figures for 2023 tell the same story: 11% of women-owned Nebraska businesses had employees, against 22% of men-owned (our arithmetic from the Census counts).<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-8" id="fnref-8-1" aria-label="Source 8">8</a></sup></p>
<p><strong>Read with care:</strong> the source counts businesses that have employees at one point in time.
It does not follow businesses over time, so it does not show how many tried to grow and could not.
Some owners choose to stay small; why the gap exists is covered under <a href="#rest-employer">the rest of the research</a>.</p>
</details>

<details class="card" id="cited-angels">
<summary>When women get in front of angel investors, <strong>27%</strong> of their deals get funded, against <strong>23%</strong> across the whole market<sup class="fn" aria-hidden="true">3</sup></summary>
<p><strong>In the pitch:</strong> slide 3 says "When women get in front of angel investors nationally, they get funded more often than average!"
The slide gives the same two figures.</p>
<p><strong>What the source says:</strong> the University of New Hampshire's Center for Venture Research estimates the US angel market each year.
For 2024 it reports that "the yield rate for women entrepreneurs seeking angel capital was 26.7%", above the 23% rate for the market as a whole.<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-3" id="fnref-3-2" aria-label="Source 3">3</a></sup>
The yield rate is the share of deals brought to angel investors that end in an investment.</p>
<p><strong>Where to find it:</strong> page 1 of the two-page report, in the part on yield rates (23%) and the part on women and minority entrepreneurs and investors (27%).</p>
<p><strong>How we checked:</strong> <span class="status status-checked">Checked</span> We read both figures in our saved copy of the report.</p>
<p><strong>Read with care:</strong> the comparison is with all deals, which include women's, not with men's deals alone.
The figures are national, not for Nebraska.
The two-page report does not give the number of deals behind each rate.
The report reads the higher rate as a sign that women's deals were of high quality.
Our pitch draws a related point: the hard part is getting in the room, not the ideas.
That second step is our reading, not the report's.</p>
</details>

<details class="card" id="cited-mentoring-trial">
<summary>In a large trial on an online mentoring platform, only <strong>14%</strong> of new users had a real back-and-forth with a mentor<sup class="fn" aria-hidden="true">9</sup></summary>
<p><strong>In the pitch:</strong> the script says "In one large experiment on an online mentoring platform, only 14% of new users had a meaningful exchange with a mentor within a few months."</p>
<p><strong>What the source says:</strong> Lall, Chen and Mason ran a randomised trial with 3,022 entrepreneurs who joined an online mentoring platform (MicroMentor) between May and August 2019.
39% started at least one conversation with a mentor, but "only 14% have developed a meaningful connection".<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-9" id="fnref-9-1" aria-label="Source 9">9</a></sup>
A meaningful connection means four or more messages in one conversation between the entrepreneur and a mentor.
Women were less likely than men to start a conversation with a mentor (a statistically significant difference in the study's main model); the study found no such difference in making a meaningful connection.
One of the trial's three approaches showed new users a video of a successful mentoring relationship.
For women, the study reports: "The chance of a female entrepreneur reaching out to a mentor is increased by 57% after she watches the video."
But the video did not raise their chance of a meaningful connection.<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-9" id="fnref-9-2" aria-label="Source 9">9</a></sup>
The 57% is a relative increase, not 57 percentage points, and it counts all women offered the video, whether or not they watched it.</p>
<p><strong>Where to find it:</strong> section 4 (Analysis), first paragraph (the 14% and 39%); section 3.2 (Variables), on what counts as a connection; Tables 3 and 4 in section 4 and the text beside them, on the difference between women and men and on the video.</p>
<p><strong>How we checked:</strong> <span class="status status-checked">Checked</span> We read the figures and the definition in our saved copy of the full article, which is open access.</p>
<p><strong>Read with care:</strong> the study describes one platform's new users, not founders in general.
The people in the study were new users of one platform, writing in English or Spanish, and 31% were women, so they are not "founders" in general.
They were followed for about three to six months, not "ever".
And 39% did start a conversation; the 14% is for an exchange of at least four messages.</p>
</details>

<details class="card" id="cited-right-person">
<summary>Our survey: the top reason a connection did not happen was "I didn't know who the right person was", for <strong>14 of 26</strong> who answered<sup class="fn" aria-hidden="true">7</sup></summary>
<p><strong>In the pitch:</strong> the script says "We surveyed 48 people in our startup network. The top reason a connection didn't happen: 'I didn't know who the right person was.'"</p>
<p><strong>What the source says:</strong> Our pilot survey had 48 responses: 23 from women, 24 from men and 1 with no gender given.
26 of them answered the question on why they could not make the connections they wanted, choosing as many reasons as applied.
14 of the 26 chose "I didn't know who the right person was", more than any other reason (women 7 of 14, men 7 of 12).<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-7" id="fnref-7-4" aria-label="Source 7">7</a></sup>
It was the most common reason among both the women and the men who answered.</p>
<p><strong>Where to find it:</strong> survey question "What was the reason you weren't able to make these connections?"</p>
<p><strong>How we checked:</strong> <span class="status status-checked">Checked</span> Counted from the survey responses by script, and the figure was checked a second time with a separate script.</p>
<p><strong>Read with care:</strong> the survey reached the team's own contacts, so these counts describe the people who answered, not all Lincoln founders.
The groups are small, so no difference between women and men here can be called a gender difference.
The 48 responses include one test response from our team; without it, this is still the most common reason.</p>
</details>

<details class="card" id="cited-mentor-wish">
<summary>Our survey: the connection people wish for most is "a mentor who's done it before", for <strong>18 of 33</strong> who answered<sup class="fn" aria-hidden="true">7</sup></summary>
<p><strong>In the pitch:</strong> slide 3 asks "What do they want most? A mentor who's done it before." The script says the same.</p>
<p><strong>What the source says:</strong> 33 people answered the question on which connections they wish they had, choosing as many as applied.
18 of the 33 chose "A mentor who's done it before", more than any other connection (women 10 of 16, men 8 of 17).<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-7" id="fnref-7-5" aria-label="Source 7">7</a></sup>
It was the most common choice among both the women and the men who answered.</p>
<p><strong>Where to find it:</strong> survey question "Which connections do you wish you had?"</p>
<p><strong>How we checked:</strong> <span class="status status-checked">Checked</span> Counted from the survey responses by script, and the figure was checked a second time with a separate script.</p>
<p><strong>Read with care:</strong> the same limits apply as for the card above: the team's own contacts, small groups, and one test response from our team, without which this is still the most common choice.</p>
</details>
</section>

<p class="note to-top"><a href="#jsr-top">Back to top</a></p>
<section id="survey" class="page-section survey" aria-labelledby="survey-title">
  <h2 id="survey-title">Survey results: what we heard in Lincoln</h2>
  <p class="lede">
    In November 2026 we ran a short pilot survey of founders, people thinking about starting a business, and the mentors, investors and program staff who support them.
    It is small and it reached people we already knew, so read every number as an illustration, not an estimate for Lincoln as a whole.<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-7" id="fnref-7-6" aria-label="Source 7">7</a></sup>
  </p>

  <div class="survey-glance" role="group" aria-labelledby="survey-glance-title">
    <h3 id="survey-glance-title">Who answered at a glance</h3>
    <div class="glance-charts">
      <figure class="bar-chart">
        <figcaption id="chart-status-cap">Where they are as founders (all 48, one group each)</figcaption>
        <svg class="bars" viewBox="0 0 260 189" width="100%" role="img" aria-labelledby="chart-status-cap" font-size="13"><g class="row"><title>Current business owners: 34 of 48</title><rect class="hit" x="0" y="0" width="260" height="37"/><text class="lbl" x="0" y="13">Current business owners</text><path class="bar" d="M0 17H224.0A4 4 0 0 1 228.0 21V24A4 4 0 0 1 224.0 28H0Z"/><text class="val" x="233.0" y="26.5">34</text></g><g class="row"><title>Former owners (business closed, sold or left): 4 of 48</title><rect class="hit" x="0" y="37" width="260" height="53"/><text class="lbl" x="0" y="50">Former owners (business closed,</text><text class="lbl" x="0" y="66">sold or left)</text><path class="bar" d="M0 70H22.8A4 4 0 0 1 26.8 74V77A4 4 0 0 1 22.8 81H0Z"/><text class="val" x="31.8" y="79.5">4</text></g><g class="row"><title>Planning to start, not yet an owner: 3 of 48</title><rect class="hit" x="0" y="90" width="260" height="53"/><text class="lbl" x="0" y="103">Planning to start, not yet an</text><text class="lbl" x="0" y="119">owner</text><path class="bar" d="M0 123H16.1A4 4 0 0 1 20.1 127V130A4 4 0 0 1 16.1 134H0Z"/><text class="val" x="25.1" y="132.5">3</text></g><g class="row"><title>Supporters or startup employees only: 7 of 48</title><rect class="hit" x="0" y="143" width="260" height="53"/><text class="lbl" x="0" y="156">Supporters or startup employees</text><text class="lbl" x="0" y="172">only</text><path class="bar" d="M0 176H42.9A4 4 0 0 1 46.9 180V183A4 4 0 0 1 42.9 187H0Z"/><text class="val" x="51.9" y="185.5">7</text></g></svg>
        <p class="chart-note">7 of 48 said they plan to start a business, including 4 current owners planning another.</p>
      </figure>
      <figure class="bar-chart">
        <figcaption id="chart-age-cap">Age (all 48)</figcaption>
        <svg class="bars" viewBox="0 0 260 141" width="100%" role="img" aria-labelledby="chart-age-cap" font-size="13"><g class="row"><title>18 to 35: 7 of 48</title><rect class="hit" x="0" y="0" width="260" height="37"/><text class="lbl" x="0" y="13">18 to 35</text><path class="bar" d="M0 17H80.0A4 4 0 0 1 84.0 21V24A4 4 0 0 1 80.0 28H0Z"/><text class="val" x="89.0" y="26.5">7</text></g><g class="row"><title>36 to 45: 19 of 48</title><rect class="hit" x="0" y="37" width="260" height="37"/><text class="lbl" x="0" y="50">36 to 45</text><path class="bar" d="M0 54H224.0A4 4 0 0 1 228.0 58V61A4 4 0 0 1 224.0 65H0Z"/><text class="val" x="233.0" y="63.5">19</text></g><g class="row"><title>46 to 55: 15 of 48</title><rect class="hit" x="0" y="74" width="260" height="37"/><text class="lbl" x="0" y="87">46 to 55</text><path class="bar" d="M0 91H176.0A4 4 0 0 1 180.0 95V98A4 4 0 0 1 176.0 102H0Z"/><text class="val" x="185.0" y="100.5">15</text></g><g class="row"><title>56 and over: 7 of 48</title><rect class="hit" x="0" y="111" width="260" height="37"/><text class="lbl" x="0" y="124">56 and over</text><path class="bar" d="M0 128H80.0A4 4 0 0 1 84.0 132V135A4 4 0 0 1 80.0 139H0Z"/><text class="val" x="89.0" y="137.5">7</text></g></svg>
      </figure>
    </div>
    <p class="gender-line">23 women and 24 men took part; 1 person did not give a gender.</p>
  </div>

  <details class="card" id="survey-who">
    <summary><span class="card-headline">Who answered</span> <span class="card-figure">48 responses</span></summary>
    <div class="card-body">
      <p>48 responses came in between 13 and 16 November 2026.<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-7" id="fnref-7-7" aria-label="Source 7">7</a></sup>
        23 women and 24 men took part; 1 person did not give a gender.
        Because that last group is so small, we show women and men separately only for questions it did not answer.</p>
      <p>People could pick more than one role:</p>
      <ul>
        <li>business owners: 38 of 48</li>
        <li>supporters (mentors, investors, program staff and service providers): 17 of 48</li>
        <li>people working at a startup: 16 of 48</li>
        <li>people planning to start a business: 7 of 48</li>
      </ul>
      <p>Where they live or work: Lincoln 32 of 48, elsewhere in Nebraska 12 of 48, outside Nebraska 4 of 48.</p>
      <p>Not everyone answered every question, so each figure below gives the number who answered that question, for example "18 of 33".</p>
    </div>
  </details>

  <h3 id="survey-findings">Headline findings</h3>

  <details class="card" id="survey-f1">
    <summary><span class="card-headline">What people want most is a mentor who has done it before</span> <span class="card-figure">18 of 33</span></summary>
    <div class="card-body">
      <p>Asked which connections they wish they had, 18 of the 33 who answered picked "a mentor who's done it before" (women 10 of 16, men 8 of 17).<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-7" id="fnref-7-8" aria-label="Source 7">7</a></sup>
        It was the most common choice, ahead of customers or distributors (16 of 33) and an investor (11 of 33).</p>
      <p>Mentors also matter in hindsight: a mentor or advisor was the most common kind of connection that mattered most to people's businesses, for 11 of 34 who answered (women 7 of 18, men 4 of 16), just ahead of another business owner (10 of 34).
        In their written answers, 12 of all 48 respondents credited a mentor or advisor with making a difference.<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-10" id="fnref-10-1" aria-label="Source 10">10</a></sup></p>
    </div>
  </details>

  <details class="card" id="survey-f2">
    <summary><span class="card-headline">The gap is knowing who to ask for the next step</span> <span class="card-figure">14 of 26</span></summary>
    <div class="card-body">
      <p>Among people who said a connection they wanted did not happen, the most common reason was "I didn't know who the right person was": 14 of the 26 who answered (women 7 of 14, men 7 of 12).<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-7" id="fnref-7-9" aria-label="Source 7">7</a></sup>
        Two reasons came next, tied at 9 of 26 each: not knowing where to find them, and feeling that events or groups were not for them.</p>
      <p>The most common obstacle overall was not being sure how to carry out the next step, such as building the product, finding customers, marketing or hiring: 14 of 35 (women 7 of 18, men 7 of 17).
        Yet 22 of 37 agree they know who to ask in their community for business help in general (women 12 of 20, men 10 of 17).
        So the gap seems to be the specific person for the specific next step, not knowing anyone at all.</p>
    </div>
  </details>

  <details class="card" id="survey-f3">
    <summary><span class="card-headline">Help comes through people</span> <span class="card-figure">24 of 48</span></summary>
    <div class="card-body">
      <p>When people wrote about what helped, the most common thread was networks and introductions: 24 of all 48 respondents.<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-10" id="fnref-10-2" aria-label="Source 10">10</a></sup>
        Next came a named program, event or grant scheme (18 of 48), then a mentor or advisor (12 of 48) and grants (10 of 48).</p>
      <p>These counts use everyone who took the survey as the base, whether or not they wrote anything, so they may undercount.
        When people credited a program, it was often for the network it gave them.</p>
    </div>
  </details>

  <details class="card" id="survey-f4">
    <summary><span class="card-headline">Programs are known, but few people use them and many do not feel they are meant for them</span> <span class="card-figure">12 of 37</span></summary>
    <div class="card-body">
      <p>Only 12 of 37 agree that local business programs are "meant for people like me" (women 4 of 20, men 8 of 17).<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-7" id="fnref-7-10" aria-label="Source 7">7</a></sup></p>
      <p>Programs are better known than used.
        StartupLNK had been heard of or used by 22 of 35 who answered (women 12 of 18, men 10 of 17), but used by fewer than 3 of 35.
        1 Million Cups had been heard of or used by 25 of 35 (women 14 of 18, men 11 of 17) and used by 12 of 35.</p>
    </div>
  </details>

  <details class="card" id="survey-f5">
    <summary><span class="card-headline">Caregiving takes up time mainly for women</span> <span class="card-figure">10 of 21 women</span></summary>
    <div class="card-body">
      <p>Caring for children or for a parent or relative takes up time for 10 of 21 women who answered, and for fewer than 3 of 19 men.<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-7" id="fnref-7-11" aria-label="Source 7">7</a></sup>
        We do not show the total for everyone here, because it would let a reader work out the exact small number for men.</p>
      <p>Most people are also fitting their business around a job: a full-time job takes up time for 32 of 40 (women 18 of 21, men 14 of 19), and not enough time is an obstacle for 11 of 35 (women 6 of 18, men 5 of 17).
        Yet fewer than 3 of 35 picked childcare or caregiving as one of their biggest obstacles, and very few wrote about their own load at home.
        The survey asked about help more than about burdens, which may be why.</p>
    </div>
  </details>

  <details class="card" id="survey-f6">
    <summary><span class="card-headline">Most owners fund their business themselves</span> <span class="card-figure">25 of 35</span></summary>
    <div class="card-body">
      <p>Personal savings fund the business for 25 of 35 who answered (women 12 of 17, men 13 of 18), and revenue from the business for 14 of 35 (women 6 of 17, men 8 of 18).<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-7" id="fnref-7-12" aria-label="Source 7">7</a></sup></p>
      <p>17 people had sought money from others, and 11 of those 17 got some or all of what they needed (women 6 of 9, men 5 of 8); that is too few answers to say how seeking money usually goes.
        Raising outside money is a goal for the next 12 months for 8 of 32 (women 3 of 17, men 5 of 15).
        In written answers, 5 of 48 described seeking money going badly, such as a bank saying no or an application not being selected.<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-10" id="fnref-10-3" aria-label="Source 10">10</a></sup></p>
    </div>
  </details>

  <details class="card" id="survey-f7">
    <summary><span class="card-headline">Help is needed after launch, not only at the start</span> <span class="card-figure">14 of 37</span></summary>
    <div class="card-body">
      <p>Growing or expanding is the stage where people most often need help: 14 of 37 who answered (women 7 of 19, men 7 of 18), ahead of legal and business setup (10 of 37).<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-7" id="fnref-7-13" aria-label="Source 7">7</a></sup>
        More customers or revenue is the most common goal for the next 12 months, for 19 of 32 (women 12 of 17, men 7 of 15).</p>
      <p>In written answers, 10 of 48 credited help with legal and accounting basics, such as an introduction to a trusted attorney or accountant.<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-10" id="fnref-10-4" aria-label="Source 10">10</a></sup></p>
    </div>
  </details>

  <details class="card" id="survey-f8">
    <summary><span class="card-headline">People feel connected, but their networks may not reach money</span> <span class="card-figure">22 of 37</span></summary>
    <div class="card-body">
      <p>22 of 37 agree that someone could introduce them to a lender or investor (women 14 of 20, men 8 of 17).<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-7" id="fnref-7-14" aria-label="Source 7">7</a></sup></p>
      <p>But among the 24 people whose written answers credited networks and introductions, 13 of 24 agree, compared with 9 of the 13 others who answered.<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-10" id="fnref-10-5" aria-label="Source 10">10</a></sup>
        That is a gap of only a few people, so treat it as an idea worth testing, not a finding.</p>
    </div>
  </details>

  <h3 id="survey-table-title">Headline figures for everyone, women and men</h3>
  <p>Each cell is the number who picked that answer out of the number in that group who answered the question.
    Counts of 1 or 2 are shown as "fewer than 3", and a few other cells are held back so that a small count cannot be worked out by subtraction.<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-7" id="fnref-7-15" aria-label="Source 7">7</a></sup></p>
  <p class="note table-hint">Scroll sideways to see all columns.</p>

  </div>
  <p class="note">The groups are small, so no difference between women and men in this table can be called a gender difference.</p>

  <details class="card" id="survey-resources">
    <summary><span class="card-headline">Local resources people used</span> <span class="card-figure">1 Million Cups 12 of 35</span></summary>
    <div class="card-body">
      <p>35 people answered the question on Lincoln and Nebraska resources; here is how many had used each one (resources used by fewer than 3 are left out).<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-7" id="fnref-7-16" aria-label="Source 7">7</a></sup></p>

      </figure>
      <p>Many more had heard of these resources than had used them: Invest Nebraska 23 of 35, LaunchLNK grants 22, StartupLNK 22, the Innovation Studio 21, BIA prototype grants 19, SCORE Lincoln 18, NBDC 18 and Nebraska Angels 18.</p>
      <p>Using a resource is not the same as saying it helped; programs people credited in their own words are counted in the themes below.</p>
    </div>
  </details>

  <h3 id="survey-themes">What people wrote</h3>

  <details class="card" id="survey-themes-card">
    <summary><span class="card-headline">Themes in the written answers</span> <span class="card-figure">37 of 48 wrote something on theme</span></summary>
    <div class="card-body">
      <p>We grouped the written answers into themes.<sup class="fn"><a href="#fn-10" id="fnref-10-6" aria-label="Source 10">10</a></sup>
        Counts are people, out of all 48 respondents, and one answer can carry several themes.
        37 of 48 wrote something that fits at least one theme.</p>
      <figure class="bar-chart bar-chart-wide">
        <figcaption id="chart-themes-cap">People out of 48 whose written answers fit each theme (themes named by 3 or more)</figcaption>
        <svg class="bars" viewBox="0 0 260 358" width="100%" role="img" aria-labelledby="chart-themes-cap" font-size="13"><g class="row"><title>Networks and introductions: 24 of 48</title><rect class="hit" x="0" y="0" width="260" height="37"/><text class="lbl" x="0" y="13">Networks and introductions</text><path class="bar" d="M0 17H224.0A4 4 0 0 1 228.0 21V24A4 4 0 0 1 224.0 28H0Z"/><text money that does not have to be paid back: 10 of 48</title><rect class="hit" x="0" y="127" width="260" height="53"/><text class="lbl" x="0" y="140">Grants and other money that does</text><text first customers or pilots: 3 of 48</title><rect class="hit" x="0" y="291" width="260" height="37"/><text class="lbl" x="0" y="304">Finding first customers or pilots</text><path class="bar" d="M0
